Consider the graph of the function $g(x),$ shown above. It consists of two line segments and an arc of a semi-circle centered at $(-1,3)$ with radius $1.$ Find the value of  ${\int }_{-4}^{3}g(x)\,\text{d}x.$

${\int }_{-4}^{3}g(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The graph consists of $3$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-4,-2],$ an arc of a semi-circle for $x\in [-2,0],$ and another line segment for $x\in [0,3].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{3}g(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{-2}g(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{0}g(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{3}g(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-2].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,0].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle with the semicircle (of radius $1$) cut out on the top, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =lw-\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =2\cdot 3-\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot {1}^{2} \\  & =6-\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,3].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =lw \\  & =3\cdot 3 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{3}g(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =18-\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
